text: An approved instruction can change in a single word.
Switch the power off... becomes switch the power on.
One word. A different instruction.
How do you catch it before release?
Meet DubGuard. Catch the one word that changes everything.
DubGuard helps industrial training teams review narration against explicit, protected instructions.
Define the reference, record or upload a take, and inspect the evidence before release. Here is the actual application.
Create a Review lets visitors bring their own script. Our reference is: switch the power off.
We protect the power state: off must remain off. On is the declared reversal.
Saving creates a temporary demo policy, not an organizationally approved instruction.
Now we select the original human recording, on-off dot wav, and preview the take.
Analyze runs the actual local CPU Whisper pipeline. The original file is preserved.
The recognized words are: switch the power on. They are provisional, with an approximate zero-to-two-second source span.
DubGuard flags a suspected polarity reversal. The actual outcome is review required, not a confirmed violation.
Open the source references and return to the original audio. Recognition is evidence to inspect, not ground truth.
The architecture starts with local audio processing, provisional transcription, and deterministic protected-rule checks.
Optional AMD Token Factory review sends script, policy, and transcript text to DeepSeek V4 Flash. Original audio stays local.
This is historical live AMD text inference: a previously authorized example, separate from the recording you just saw.
The saved response cites the off-on reversal, with two validated source spans and zero citation issues.
Model advice remains advisory. Citation validation leads back to human evidence review.
Back in the application, a reviewer can replay the original and inspect the recognized words.
Spoken evidence should be corrected only after listening. This capture leaves human confirmation pending.
A temporary note preserves the need for further review. Export retains the evidence for inspection.
Demo decisions are separate from authenticated organizational sign-off.
Off and on. Fifteen and fifty. Before and after. Small changes deserve careful review.
Local speech transcription. Protected instruction checks. AMD-assisted semantic review. Source-linked evidence. Human-controlled decisions.
DubGuard is a review aid. Critical or unresolved evidence must never become automatic approval.
DubGuard. Catch the one word that changes everything.
